disease_label_per_paper: Philadelphia chromosome-positive B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia presenting with extreme hyperleukocytosis and leukostasis
presentation_summary: 22-year-old man referred after hyperleukocytosis was found during evaluation of persistent local foot swelling after an insect bite.
He had fatigue, hair loss, hepatomegaly, splenomegaly, WBC 542 x10^9/L, hemoglobin 10.2 g/dL, platelets 99 x10^9/L, LDH 425 U/L, and 80% lymphoblasts on peripheral smear.

There were no initial signs of tumor lysis, but he developed mild somnolence and blurred vision with fundoscopic retinal venous dilation, tortuosity, and punctate hemorrhages compatible with leukostasis.
Leukocytapheresis on two consecutive days reduced WBC to 211 x10^9/L with symptom relief; Ph-positive B-ALL was confirmed by marrow/flow/molecular testing.
